title: Arancini
subtitle: Crispy fried risotto balls stuffed with molten mozzarella
excerpt: Arancini are the best thing you can do with leftover risotto. A cube of mozzarella hidden in the centre melts as they fry, giving a stretchy core inside the golden crust.
sourceNotes: Arancini originated in Sicily and are now found across Italy. The name means 'little oranges', referring to their colour and shape after frying.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked, crumbed arancini on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Fry from frozen, adding 3 to 4 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the risotto base the day before and refrigerate. Cold risotto is easier to shape.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil temperature for frying: 175C. Use a probe thermometer.

content.text: Cold risotto shapes far more easily than warm. If you make the risotto base the night before, rolling the arancini takes half the time. Keep the mozzarella cubes small so they sit centred inside each ball.

items.prepNote: kept hot in a separate pan

content.text: Soften the onion in butter in a large saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir to coat. Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting until each ladleful is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18 minutes.
Stir in the Parmesan. Season well. Spread the risotto on a tray and cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Divide the cold risotto into 12 portions. Flatten each into a disc in your palm. Place a mozzarella cube in the centre and wrap the rice around it to form a ball. Press firmly to seal.
Set up a coating station: beaten egg in one bowl, breadcrumbs in another. Dip each ball in egg, then roll in breadcrumbs until fully coated.
Heat the sunflower oil in a deep saucepan to 175C. Fry the arancini 3 or 4 at a time for 4 to 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown.
Drain on kitchen paper. Eat within 10 minutes while the mozzarella centre is still molten.

items.symptom: The arancini fall apart during frying.
items.cause: The risotto was too wet or the balls were not pressed firmly enough.
items.fix: Chill the shaped balls for 30 minutes before frying.

items.symptom: The crust is dark but the centre is still cold.
items.cause: The oil temperature was too high.
items.fix: Lower oil to 165C and fry for longer.

items.symptom: The mozzarella has not melted inside.
items.cause: The cubes were too large or the frying time too short.
items.fix: Cut mozzarella smaller and fry for 1 to 2 more minutes.
